<Link to="/contact" className="button-primary">Book a consultation</Link>

The test uses getByRole('link', { name: /book a consultation/i }). The Link component renders an <a> element, role is link by default. However we added role="button" attribute? Let's check: In Home page at CTA band we have <Link to="/contact" className="button-primary" role="button">Book a consultation</Link>. That's role button, not link. Also in hero we have <Link to="/contact" className="button-primary">Book a consultation</Link> (no role). That one is a link.

But test picks any link with name "Book a consultation". The hero link should match. However test fails: It cannot find link with name "book a consultation". Perhaps because the hero link appears but the test maybe after rendering sees only the link for the CTA? Wait the component renders both hero link and CTA band link (both same text). However the test expects a link with name /book a consultation/i, but the link we have is there. Why not found? The output shows that available links are: "The Bayes Group home", "Services", "Training", "About". No "Book a consultation". So the hero link is missing? Maybe because we added aria-label to Wordmark linking to home, causing missing? But more likely the Link element for hero is not visible due to CSS maybe? No, test only queries role and name; if element exists with accessible name "Book a consultation". The Link text is correct. However maybe we need to set the link to have role="link"? By default <a> is link; but maybe our CSS makes it display:none? Not.

But the test also later finds ctaBtn = screen.getByRole('link', { name: /book a consultation/i }) at the end, which passes earlier? The earlier part fails. It fails at hero stage before reaching CTA? Actually they get hero button using getByRole('link', { name: /book a consultation/i }). This should match any link with that text. Since we have two such links, should succeed.

Maybe the Link component from react-router-dom, when rendered without 'role' attribute, it still renders <a>. So role is link. Should work.

But the output shows only four links: The Bayes Group home (wordmark link), Services, Training, About. No Contact link displayed. Why Contact link not present? In Home, we have hero link but maybe the Header's Book a consultation link overrides something? However the test only queries within the entire document, not specific region. It didn't find any link to /contact.

Maybe the issue is that we changed the Header to include a "Book a consultation" link with role="button" and style, but we also removed the navigation links? - R5: To test CSS variable value, need to examine computed style of an element that uses var(--color-accent). We can query root element (document.documentElement) for computed style of property '--color-accent', but be careful that CSS variables are not resolved in computed style of document.documentElement; they are accessible via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--color-accent'), which returns the defined value with possible whitespace. So test that getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--color-accent') trimmed equals "#1F8A8A". However spec says accent color defined in CSS custom properties is "#166666" instead of "#1F8A8A". So the test should fail on current code (i.e., code likely defines incorrectly). We want to test that it equals "#1F8A8A". Use toBe('#1F8A8A') after trimming. This is a simple test.

If the CSS variable is defined somewhere else (maybe src/index.css). But we can query root.

Potential nuance: getComputedStyle returns value like "#1F8A8A" or it might be "#1F8A8A " with trailing whitespace; use .trim().

Actually JSX files are .tsx, compiled via TypeScript; the code should be valid JSX with Unicode characters allowed – but the file is being run via Python's run_python (executing as Python), not compiled. The static validation runs npm install, npm run build, which succeeded earlier, meaning the TypeScript compiled fine. But the test runner (jest) uses ts-jest to compile .tsx, so those characters are okay. The errors we see are from trying to run the file using Python runner, which treats them as Python code, causing syntax error. That's irrelevant; the tests used jest with ts-jest, not Python. So we shouldn't evaluate using run_python.

The failing test is m2-home.test expecting two book links; Received only one. Let's inspect Home page code: In hero, there is a Link with class button-primary, role button, text Book a consultation. In cta band, there is also a Link class button-primary with text Book a consultation. Both should be found. However test counts links inside main region. Perhaps the cta band is not inside <main>. In Home component, the outermost div className="container". There's no <main> element. In App.tsx likely wraps routes with <main>. Let's open App.tsx.
